from pysat.solvers import Solver
from pysat.formula import CNF

# Graph definition
n_vertices = 37
n_colors = 4

edges = [
    (0,4), (0,27), (0,30), (0,34), (1,19), (1,26), (2,16), (2,17), (2,35),
    (3,9), (3,12), (3,25), (3,29), (3,30), (3,36), (4,15), (4,21), (4,24),
    (4,36), (5,10), (5,11), (5,13), (5,15), (5,17), (5,20), (5,29), (6,10),
    (6,17), (6,21), (7,14), (7,24), (7,25), (7,28), (7,33), (8,13), (8,26),
    (8,32), (8,33), (8,35), (9,12), (9,19), (9,23), (9,25), (9,30), (9,34),
    (10,19), (10,22), (10,31), (11,30), (11,35), (12,16), (12,17), (12,21),
    (12,29), (12,33), (13,15), (13,19), (13,27), (13,31), (13,32), (13,35),
    (14,15), (14,19), (14,22), (14,25), (14,28), (14,29), (14,32), (14,36),
    (15,24), (15,25), (15,28), (15,29), (15,30), (15,33), (15,35), (16,18),
    (16,21), (17,28), (17,35), (17,36), (18,20), (18,22), (18,36), (19,35),
    (20,24), (20,34), (21,25), (22,34), (23,32), (23,36), (24,28), (24,29),
    (24,30), (24,33), (24,34), (26,31), (26,32), (27,35), (28,33), (29,36),
    (30,35), (31,32), (31,36), (33,35)
]

# Variable encoding: var(v, c) = v * n_colors + c + 1
def var(v, c):
    return v * n_colors + c + 1

cnf = CNF()

# Each vertex must have at least one color
for v in range(n_vertices):
    cnf.append([var(v, c) for c in range(n_colors)])

# Each vertex has at most one color
for v in range(n_vertices):
    for c1 in range(n_colors):
        for c2 in range(c1+1, n_colors):
            cnf.append([-var(v, c1), -var(v, c2)])

# Adjacent vertices must have different colors
for (u, v) in edges:
    for c in range(n_colors):
        cnf.append([-var(u, c), -var(v, c)])

# Solve
solver = Solver(name='g3')
solver.append_formula(cnf)
result = solver.solve()

if result:
    model = solver.get_model()
    coloring = []
    for v in range(n_vertices):
        for c in range(n_colors):
            if var(v, c) in model:
                coloring.append(c)
                break
    print("SAT")
    print("Coloring:", coloring)
    
    # Verify
    valid = True
    for (u, v) in edges:
        if coloring[u] == coloring[v]:
            print(f"CONFLICT: edge ({u},{v}) both color {coloring[u]}")
            valid = False
    if valid:
        print("Verification: VALID coloring")
else:
    print("UNSAT")
